This diagram illustrates the architecture and data flow of a Reversible Lane Control System (RLCS) integrated with other traffic management systems. The central component is the RLCS, which communicates bidirectionally via solid lines (existing connections) with several key elements:

- **Reversible Lane Changeable Message Signs**: Receives “Message Number Control Commands” and sends back “Device Status”.
- **Reversible Lane Field Devices** (gates, pop-up, lights): Receives “Device Control Commands” and sends back “Device Status”.
- **RLCS Operator**: Exchanges “RLCS Status and Control” information.
- **External Server**: Connected bidirectionally; also receives dashed-line (future) inputs from ATMS and Value Pricing systems labeled “RLCS Lane Status” and “RLCS Customers”.

The RLCS also connects via dashed lines (future interfaces) to:
- **Ramp Metering**: Sends “RLCS Lane Status” and “RLCS Customers”; Ramp Metering in turn controls “Ramp Meters (Model 170 Controllers)” — 300 devices — by sending them “Ramp Meter Rates”. Ramp Metering also receives “Loop Detector Data (volume and occupancy)” from Loop Detectors (1,200–1,800 devices).
- **ATIS (Advanced Traveler Information System)**: Receives “Traveler Information” from RLCS and broadcasts it via “Broadcast Traveler Info” tower.
- **Value Pricing (Managed Lanes)**: Exchanges “RLCS Lane Status” and “RLCS Customers” with RLCS; also outputs “Lane Status and Vehicle Charge” to “FasTrak Changeable Message Signs”.

On the left side, the **ATMS (Advanced Traffic Management System)** acts as a hub for surveillance and workstation data:
- Receives “Video and Camera Control” from “Video Surveillance” cameras.
- Receives “Loop Detector Data (volume and occupancy)” from Loop Detectors (same 1,200–1,800 devices feeding Ramp Metering).
- Distributes “Video and Loop Detector Data” to three workstations:
  - “ATMS Workstation (CHP)”
  - “ATMS Workstation (Caltrans Traffic Operations)”
  - “ATMS Workstation” (unspecified agency)
- Also has future (dashed) connections to External Server (“RLCS Lane Status”, “RLCS Customers”) and to Ramp Metering (“RLCS Lane Status”, “RLCS Customers”).

Legend indicates:
- Solid curved arrows = Existing connections
- Dashed curved arrows = Future connections

All components are interconnected to support real-time control, monitoring, traveler information, and managed lane pricing within a reversible lane infrastructure.

The table defines six user classes and their associated system functions:

1. **Operator**: Has command control of the system during normal mode. Only one ‘operator’ may be logged onto the system at any given time. Authorized to change system mode.

2. **Management**: Limited to reporting and status checking capabilities only.

3. **Field Maintenance Staff**: Has command control of the system only during maintenance mode. Can execute maintenance mode control sequences from FCU workstations, remote dial-in terminals, or the maintenance building workstation — but not from the TMC workstation. Not able to change system mode.

4. **Electrical Systems (Hardware)**: Restricted to reporting and status checking.

5. **Software Systems (Software)**: Also restricted to reporting and status checking.

6. **System Administrator**: A member of the District 11 technical staff (usually a Software Systems staff member) authorized to create and modify system configuration data — including staff, devices, and scheduled operations. Also authorized to change system mode.

00e3ac15706ed9ff7e6748ac321a07de15fff302: For a system with 205 sensors, each status command requires 200 bytes. When the polling interval is set to 2 seconds, the transmission rate is 164 kbits/second. When the polling interval is increased to 30 seconds, the transmission rate decreases to 10.9 kbits/second. The number of sensors and bytes per status command remain constant at 205 and 200 respectively in both scenarios.
69aff9217d5af691ab6a23575c60fca8954dfd00: For fewer than 205 sensors, each control command requires 200 bytes. With 4 control commands issued per day, the total daily data volume for control commands is calculated as (200 × 205 × 4 × 8) / 1000, which equals less than 1,312 kilobits.

The table lists 39 entities with their minimum required attributes, organized by entity number and name. Each entity represents a distinct data object or concept within a system, likely for traffic management, device control, or operational logging.

1. **Agency**: Requires Agency ID, Agency Name, Contact, Address, and Phone.
2. **Alarm Type**: Defined by Alarm Type ID and Description (with examples: critical, warning).
3. **Command Level**: Includes Command Level ID, Name (examples: status, control, override), and type (status/control).
4. **Customer Type**: Contains Customer Type ID and Name (examples: general public, FasTrak, HOV).
5. **Device**: Must include Device ID, Name, Device Status ID, graphic image for display, location ID, direction, Device Category ID, and Last Maintenance Date.
6. **Device Alarm Criteria**: Comprises Device Alarm Criteria ID, Device ID, Alarm low range, Alarm high range, Alarm Description, and Device Status ID.
7. **Device Category**: Defined by Device Category ID, Name, and Description of category.
8. **Device Command**: Includes Device Command ID, Device ID, Command String, Timeout, and Command Level.
9. **Device Command Macro**: Contains Device Command Macro ID, Device ID, Command Name, Command String, Timeout, and Command Level.
10. **Device Command Log**: Records Device Command Log ID, Device Command ID, Date, Time, Device Status ID, and Operator ID.
11. **Device Command Steps**: Consists of Device Command Steps ID, Device Command ID, Step #, and Device Command.
12. **Device Rules**: Includes Device Rules ID, Mode, Device X desired status, and Device Y prohibited status.
13. **Device Status**: Defined by Device Status ID, Name, and Description of status (e.g., ok, alarm).

15. **Emergency Notification Profile**: Includes Emergency Notification Profile ID, Schedule Shift, Alarm Type ID, Personnel ID, Pager #, and Telephone #.
16. **Location**: Requires Location ID, Highway #, Segment, Direction, Lane #, geo code, and Name.
17. **Operator Daily Diary Log**: Records Operator Daily Diary Log ID, Personnel ID, Date, and Notes.
18. **Personnel**: Includes Personnel ID, Name, Initials for login, password, and password date.
19. **Personnel Classification**: Defined by Personnel Classification ID, Name, and Description of classification.
20. **Personnel Security Level**: Contains Personnel Security Level ID, Mode, Functions, Command Level, Devices, and Workstation.

25. **Personnel Workstations**: Connects Personnel ID and Workstation ID.
26. **Problem Work Order**: Contains Problem Work Order ID, Date, Time, Operator, Problem Work Order Status ID, and Description.

28. **Problem Work Order Status**: Defined by Problem Work Order Status ID, Name, and Description of status.

The table defines key terms related to the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System (RLCS), as follows:

- **DCU** stands for Device Control Unit.
- **Device Override** is the system’s capability allowing a properly secured operator to continue an operating sequence to completion despite any intermediate device control failure, by manually inputting a device status that overrides the field-reported status.
- **Facility** refers to the physical roadway of the I-15 reversible lane, including all associated field devices, electronic components, and software used to monitor and control those field devices.
- **FCU** stands for Field Control Unit.
- **Field Devices** include gates, pop-ups, CMS (Changeable Message Signs), lights, loop detectors, power systems, pressure transducers, and any other controlled device.
- **MCU** stands for Manual Control Unit.
- **Operational Override** is the system’s capability allowing a properly secured operator to issue device commands outside of a predetermined operational event, on demand.
- **PIER** stands for Post Implementation Evaluation Review.
- **RLCS** stands for The I-15 Reversible Lane Control System — specifically, the electronic components and software used to monitor and control field devices within the I-15 Reversible Lane Facility. It may refer to either the existing or proposed RLCS.
- **TEES** stands for Transportation Electrical Equipment Specification.
- **TMC** stands for Traffic Management Center.
- **TSU** stands for Traffic Systems Unit.

All definitions are presented as stated in the source table, with no additional facts inferred or added.
